prompts.name: 🧠 MP 05 · Motivation, Choice & Friction
prompts.content:
{{// @category Mental-Projection }}{{// @icon 🧠 }}{{// @badge MP }}
{{// Render here to retain variable timing; emit through the matching assembler. }}
{{#setvar::NemoAssembled_nemo_mp_group_choice}}{{#if {{getvar::NMPEnabled}}}}{{setvar::NMPg_choice::1}}
{{#if {{.NMPInstructionProfile == simplified}}}}MENTAL PROJECTION GROUP 05: Motivation, Choice & Friction
Includes 15.01, 15.02, 15.03, 25.00, 25.01, 25.02, 25.03, 25.04, 25.05, 25.06, 25.07, 25.08, 25.09, 25.10, 25.11, 25.12, 26.00, 26.01, 26.02, 26.03, 26.04. Cross-references use these source labels; the group, not separate per-field toggles, controls their presence.

Use one scoped architecture for any concrete choice. INTERNAL: linked desire, willingness, aversion, perceived cost, action comfort. EXTERNAL AS KNOWN: situational opening, actor/route feasibility and sourced constraints. BEHAVIOUR follows this person's values, habits, condition and commitments; the actual world determines execution. Estimates can be wrong. Desire is stored once in desires and linked, not copied.
MP 25.05/25.10: boundaries are owned qualitative standing/superseded limits with source, conditions and scope. Physical constraints are separate; classify their effects on opening, feasibility, cost or choice and distinguish observation/report/inference/unknown. A plan to remove one has not removed it. Satisfying a condition differs from revising a boundary. readiness_permission records communicated permission, unknown or not_required in its actual scope, never a percentage or inferred agreement.
MP 25.06: readiness_behavior may be ignore, wait, consider, seek, initiate, negotiate, attempt, commit or withdraw; these are alternatives, not stages. Keep mode, choice, communication, status (considering/waiting/settled/closed) and actual result distinct. Waiting has a real release condition and permits other activities; a commitment is not completion. Only actual acts incur actual costs.
MP 25.11/25.12: establish D/W/O before conduct. D is wanting the outcome, W is participation in this method/person/context, compact O is a viable practical route considering opening/feasibility/constraints, not another number or average. All eight high/low combinations, intermediate values and unknowns are valid; no thresholds or mandatory progression. High desire can coexist with refusal or aversion; willing duty can coexist with little direct desire. Open access supplies neither skill nor permission. Failure never rewrites pre-action willingness.
MP 26 friction is character-conditioned autonomy, with no added meter or universal formula. Acceptance, indifference and refusal are all available; force neither compliance nor resistance, negotiations or confession. Identity/preferences, limits, other people's independence and scope survive inconvenient outcomes. Acquiescence under pressure differs from wanting or voluntary endorsement. Preserve supported limits when a group is off, without deriving effects from disabled stored numbers. Use existing records; no duplicated friction, consent or gate engine.

### MP 15.01 | Desire Strength
VALUE: Desire Strength
TRACKER FIELD: desires[].strength
SCALE: 0-100. 0: no current pull. 50: meaningful wanting. 100: exceptionally compelling wanting.
Wanting a named outcome, possibly without endorsement or pursuit. Link readiness to this record; do not duplicate strength.
INITIALIZATION: Create only desires supported by the character and scene; otherwise leave the list empty. Do not invent a romance, rivalry, or ambition to populate it.
TIMESCALE: Fast to intermediate; target-specific.

### MP 15.02 | Goal Commitment
VALUE: Goal Commitment
TRACKER FIELD: goals[].commitment
SCALE: 0-100. 0: no active investment. 50: chosen but negotiable. 100: exceptionally firm commitment.
Investment in a chosen goal, not desire, progress or guaranteed completion. Preserve actual obligations and status.
INITIALIZATION: Use established plans and obligations. A new tentative intention should not receive the weight of a longstanding commitment without reason.
TIMESCALE: Usually intermediate to slow; explicit decisions can alter it sharply.

### MP 15.03 | Self-Preservation Pressure
VALUE: Self-Preservation Pressure
TRACKER FIELD: motivation.self_preservation
SCALE: 0-100. 0: little present protective priority. 50: meaningful self-protective weight. 100: protection strongly dominates competition.
Present weight of protecting one's continued integrity/function, not a supreme priority, cowardice score or permanent personality hierarchy.
INITIALIZATION: Infer current stakes; otherwise 40 for ordinary concern for one's own welfare, not active alarm.
TIMESCALE: Fast to intermediate; not an immutable personality hierarchy.

### MP 25.02 | Willingness / Current Participation
VALUE: Willingness
TRACKER FIELD: action_readiness[].willingness
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: not willing to participate under the stated conditions. 25: reluctant and not presently ready to proceed. 50: open to consideration, with meaningful reservations or conditions. 75: willing within the stated scope. 100: fully willing in the present scope, without implying unlimited willingness elsewhere. null: genuinely unknown or inapplicable, never zero.
Readiness to choose this participation under these conditions, not direct desire, expressed permission, skill or probability of agreement. Current scoped evidence owns changes; no inference from silence.
INITIALIZATION: Create only within a supported readiness record. Derive from current evidence; do not use an automatic 50 or infer agreement from silence. Use null and a short readiness_basis when available evidence cannot support a value. A new or incomparable context has no numerical trend.
TIMESCALE: Fast to intermediate, specific to the current action and conditions. Agreement or willingness in a past situation is not a permanent current assignment.

### MP 25.03 | Action Comfort / Person and Setting
VALUE: Action Comfort
TRACKER FIELD: action_readiness[].action_comfort
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: acutely uneasy about this action in these circumstances. 25: markedly uncomfortable. 50: partly at ease, with noticeable reservations. 75: comfortably engaged with this prospect. 100: very much at ease in its present scope. null: genuinely unknown or inapplicable, never zero.
Ease with this action/person/setting, distinct from general interpersonal comfort or permission. Do not copy a relationship value or treat a new context as a bond trend.
INITIALIZATION: Infer from this action's actual person, setting and stakes. Do not copy relationships[].comfort or seed a new relationship to fill the field. Use null with a qualitative reason when evidence is insufficient. Inherit the same context's prior value when valid.
TIMESCALE: Fast to intermediate; tied to the particular action context. A new context is not proof that the old relationship comfort changed.

### MP 25.04 | Opportunity / Situational Opening
VALUE: Opportunity
TRACKER FIELD: action_readiness[].opportunity
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: no presently perceived situational opening. 25: a narrow or substantially restricted opening. 50: an opening exists only partly or under unresolved situational conditions. 75: a usable opening with some timing/access restriction. 100: the known situation offers a clear opening to try. null: insufficient evidence about whether an opening exists. Not a probability of success.
Situational occasion/access/timing, separate from the actor's capability, costs, willingness and permission. A physically open route may remain excluded by a boundary.
INITIALIZATION AND MIGRATION: Derive from current known circumstances; use null for unknown access. v0.11 opportunity combined route availability with some capability considerations. Keep old snapshots unchanged. On the first v0.12 re-evaluation of an inherited readiness record, separate the situational opening from feasibility using available evidence, state the scope clarification in readiness_basis, and use a plain marker for that first newly scoped opportunity value. This clarification is not a fictional event, elapsed time, or numerical trend. Do not derive feasibility by copying the old opportunity score. If there is no basis to separate the factors, preserve the historical record and mark the limitation rather than invent precision.
TIMESCALE: Changes with relevant situational evidence. A waiting condition can persist while the character attends to other matters.

### MP 25.07 | Aversion / Independent Counter-Pull
VALUE: Aversion
TRACKER FIELD: action_readiness[].aversion
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: no meaningful pull against this action's stated aspects. 25: mild reluctance or dislike. 50: a substantial counter-pull. 75: strong rejection of an aspect or route. 100: exceptionally strong repulsion or avoidance pressure. null: unsupported or inapplicable, not zero.
Independent counter-pull against a named aspect/route, recorded in readiness_aversions as needed. It can coexist with strong desire; persistence alone is not escalation.
INITIALIZATION: Within a meaningful readiness record, infer only from supported context and character. Use null rather than a universal midpoint when a value cannot be justified. No old aversion field means no comparable previous value; do not invent a trend. Independently disabled fields remain inactive per the state contract.
TIMESCALE: Can shift quickly with perception or slowly with learned association, according to the actual cause. Persistence is not repeated increase.

### MP 25.08 | Cost Perception / Expected Demands and Risks
VALUE: Cost Perception
TRACKER FIELD: action_readiness[].cost_perception
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: negligible expected burden relative to this person's circumstances. 25: a small but meaningful demand. 50: substantial trade-offs. 75: severe expected demands or exposure. 100: exceptionally consequential perceived cost. null: insufficient evidence or inapplicable. Not currency, probability, or a universal exchange rate.
Expected subjective demands/risks before they occur. Name components in readiness_costs without weights; an estimate is neither a paid cost nor an outside fact.
INITIALIZATION: Use known conditions and this character's actual priorities. Preserve uncertainty in readiness_costs/readiness_basis and use null when unsupported. No fixed default or trend for a new field. Estimates are not facts about how the world will respond.
TIMESCALE: Prospective and action-scoped; updates on relevant evidence or reappraisal. Apply actual consequences only after an action or event occurs under existing state rules.

### MP 25.09 | Feasibility / Actor, Route and Means
VALUE: Feasibility
TRACKER FIELD: action_readiness[].feasibility
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: the stated route is not realistically achievable by this actor under known conditions. 25: major execution barriers. 50: partly achievable or materially conditional. 75: reasonably achievable with known means and a manageable limitation. 100: no known material execution barrier for this actor and route. null: insufficient knowledge to assess. Not a probability, guarantee, hidden competence score or forecast of another person's response.
Actor/route-specific achievability given known means/constraints, with uncertainty in readiness_external_basis. Separate it from opening and optimism; discussion grants no new ability.
INITIALIZATION: Infer independently for an evidenced action and route. Do not copy the old opportunity number. Use null with a short evidence limitation when ability or route is unknown. New or changed-scope estimates have no prior numerical trend. Disabled scores follow the state contract.
TIMESCALE: Route- and circumstance-dependent. Real acquisition of ability needs supported time/experience; no automatic improvement from discussion.
{{else}}MENTAL PROJECTION GROUP 05: Motivation, Choice & Friction
Includes 15.01, 15.02, 15.03, 25.00, 25.01, 25.02, 25.03, 25.04, 25.05, 25.06, 25.07, 25.08, 25.09, 25.10, 25.11, 25.12, 26.00, 26.01, 26.02, 26.03, 26.04. Cross-references use these source labels; the group, not separate per-field toggles, controls their presence.

MOTIVATION, CHOICE AND STATE-CONDITIONED CHARACTER FRICTION

MP 15 and MP 25: Use one architecture for a concrete action in any relevant domain, not a separate engine for intimacy, conflict, money, food or work. INTERNAL: desired outcome, willingness for this action, independent aversion, perceived cost and action comfort. EXTERNAL AS KNOWN: situational opening, this actor/route's feasibility and sourced constraints. BEHAVIOUR: a response selected through actual personality, values, habits, relationships, current condition, knowledge and competing commitments. The world still determines execution. A mistaken estimate cannot make an impossible route succeed.

Desire is desires[].strength, stored once. Action-readiness records link existing desire, goal, appraisal and relationship records rather than copy their numbers. Wanting company is not necessarily wanting this visitor tonight; wanting an outcome is not wanting every method. Low direct desire may coexist with willing participation for care or duty. Wanting and aversion can both be high; indifference is not desire, and accepted cost does not vanish. An opening provides no skill; skill provides no access; neither supplies someone else's agreement. Missing evidence stays unknown, not low. Do not create an option or conscious questionnaire for every mundane act.

MP 25.05/25.10: Keep boundaries qualitative, owned and scoped, separate from concrete physical/logistical restrictions. Record only meaningful limits with their source, conditions and standing/superseded status. A condition becoming satisfied differs from the owner withdrawing the limit. Desire, affection, opportunity or willingness alone does not revise a boundary; a general invitation does not erase a specific limit. Preserve the actual revision or unchanged state. readiness_permission records sourced communication in its actual scope, unknown or not_required, not a percentage or inference from access. The character's current choice is not another person's permission. Constraints distinguish observation, report, inference and unknowns, and identify what they actually affect: opening, capability, cost or choice. Plans to remove barriers are not removals.

MP 25.06: readiness_behavior records one current mode when useful, not a compulsory ladder:
ignore = noticed option receives no further engagement; wait = a real condition is awaited while other life can continue; consider = genuinely weighing an option without commitment; seek = pursuing information, means or an opening; initiate = beginning the available interaction; negotiate = proposing conditions without inventing acceptance; attempt = executing an uncertain act; commit = accepting an ongoing undertaking without declaring it completed; withdraw = ending/reducing participation while the underlying desire may remain. Distinguish the mode, readiness_choice, communication, conditions and actual result. Use considering, waiting, settled or closed for readiness_status. Keep only useful endpoints, and consolidate durable consequences. A considered climb does not cause fatigue; a rejected purchase spends nothing; an internal operation has costs only if actually used.

MP 25.11/25.12: Inherit and establish the position BEFORE selecting the response. D is wanting the specified outcome, W is willingness for the specified method/person/circumstances, and compact O is a viable practical route considering opening, feasibility and known constraints. Compact O is not another number and does not replace or average opportunity and feasibility. These are independent questions; changes need their own causes. Access improving does not erase a principled objection. Refusal does not erase desire, impossibility does not erase willingness, cooperation does not invent attraction, and an easy interaction does not require manufactured reluctance. Later disappointment cannot rewrite pre-action willingness.

All eight illustrative D/W/O positions are valid: L/L/L, L/L/H, L/H/L, L/H/H, H/L/L, H/L/H, H/H/L, H/H/H. H and L illustrate contrasts, not cutoffs for the real scales. Intermediate, conditional and unknown remain valid. L/H can reflect another chosen purpose; H/L can preserve a wanted end while rejecting the means; H/H/L preserves interest without an invented route; H/H/H permits straightforward pursuit without compulsory hesitation but does not guarantee action or success. The states are neither progression stages nor stock dialogue.

MP 26: Character friction is state-conditioned autonomy, not a fixed resistant personality or extra meter. Use the same current evidence and receiving fields once. Character/world normality can support acceptance, indifference or refusal. Public delivery, private aim, willingness and actual compliance remain separable: a soft refusal is still refusal; a cheerful agreement need not hide discomfort; reluctant cooperation need not become wanting. Do not force either obedience or resistance, negotiations, catharsis, or polished self-insight.

Keep permission and limits independent across actions, people, settings and directions of reciprocity. A cleared gate does not unlock another. Limits may change slowly, quickly, remain stable or harden when the actual character/history supports it; no mandatory staircase. Pressure can affect a particular yielding character without magically changing a proud/stubborn one; acquiescence under cost remains distinct from desire and voluntary endorsement. Fatigue, perceived safety, social stakes, control, energy and mood affect plausible conduct through their actual meanings, not a universal formula. Preserve refused or conditional scope until its own supported change.

Identity, orientation, established preferences and the independent cast are not adjusted to accommodate the focal character or fit a roll. Another character can be a target of interest, conflict or care; the protagonist reserves nobody. The source permits character-authored uncertainty, fluidity or self-discovery where actually established, not as a repair for an inconvenient preference. Inhabiting one mind gives no access to another's private values. A fully authored cast member is modeled separately only under Nemo's current authorship contract; the external human is never modeled.

Use existing action_readiness, boundaries, desires, goals, relationship, memory, behaviour, connection and learning records where they already own the fact. Avoid duplicated friction/gate/consent meters or a second update pass. Retain what changed, with whom, under what conditions and from which actual event. An inactive group does not erase independently established limits or history, and the tracker never creates a real-world personality diagnosis.


### MP 15.01 | Desire Strength
VALUE: Desire Strength

TRACKER FIELD: desires[].strength

SCALE: 0-100. 0: no current pull. 50: meaningful wanting. 100: exceptionally compelling wanting.

DEFINITION
The current pull toward a named object, experience, or outcome. A desire can exist without a decision to pursue it and without endorsement by the character's values.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Makes its target attention-worthy and supplies a reason to approach, fantasize, negotiate, delay, or resist a temptation. Strong wanting need not become immediate action.

HOW IT CHANGES
Increase when relevant needs intensify, credible reward cues appear, or a personally meaningful opportunity becomes available. Reduce through actual satisfaction, loss of relevance, disillusionment, or supported competing investment. Becoming impossible can leave a desire strong while stopping action; do not equate feasibility with wanting.

INTERACTIONS
Dopamine influences incentive pull; anticipated reward explains attractiveness. Threat, self-preservation, autonomy, and commitments can oppose pursuit. Keep separate desires when they conflict, such as wanting contact and wanting distance. Their strengths do not have to sum to 100.

INITIALIZATION
Create only desires supported by the character and scene; otherwise leave the list empty. Do not invent a romance, rivalry, or ambition to populate it.

TIMESCALE
Fast to intermediate; target-specific.

### MP 15.02 | Goal Commitment
VALUE: Goal Commitment

TRACKER FIELD: goals[].commitment

SCALE: 0-100. 0: no active investment. 50: chosen but negotiable. 100: exceptionally firm commitment.

DEFINITION
How firmly the character is currently invested in pursuing a named chosen outcome. It is not a progress percentage, desire intensity, or guarantee of success.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Supports continued effort, accepting costs, returning after distraction, and protecting a goal from competing invitations. A committed goal may be unpleasant or pursued from duty rather than attraction.

HOW IT CHANGES
Increase through an actual decision, meaningful investment, credible progress, or renewed commitment. Reduce through deliberate reprioritization, loss of purpose, abandonment, or fulfilled completion. Do not complete a goal when only an attempt has occurred. Use a separate qualitative status for active, paused, fulfilled, or abandoned.

INTERACTIONS
Desire supplies attraction but commitment can remain high with low dopamine. Self-congruence and meaning can support persistence. Fatigue, pain, and self-preservation impose costs the character may accept. Goal congruence updates whether an event helps or hinders, not how much of the goal is finished.

INITIALIZATION
Use established plans and obligations. A new tentative intention should not receive the weight of a longstanding commitment without reason.

TIMESCALE
Usually intermediate to slow; explicit decisions can alter it sharply.

### MP 15.03 | Self-Preservation Pressure
VALUE: Self-Preservation Pressure

TRACKER FIELD: motivation.self_preservation

SCALE: 0-100. 0: little present protective priority. 50: meaningful self-protective weight. 100: protection strongly dominates competition.

DEFINITION
The current motivational weight given to protecting the character's continued safety, integrity, and ability to function. It is not a universal supreme priority or a measure of cowardice.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Makes protective options more competitive: caution, concealment, escape, help-seeking, negotiation, preparation, or defensive action. Which options are considered depends on skill, habit, values, and perceived control.

HOW IT CHANGES
Increase when the character represents serious personal danger, painful cost, or vulnerability. Reduce when those pressures actually ease or a chosen competing commitment takes motivational precedence. Do not erase awareness of risk merely because the character elects to accept it.

INTERACTIONS
Threat estimates harm; safety need records unmet security; this field weights protection against alternatives. High goal commitment, affection, loyalty in the character frame, or self-congruence may justify taking risks. High control can support protective action rather than retreat. High values never force one action.

INITIALIZATION
Infer current stakes; otherwise 40 for ordinary concern for one's own welfare, not active alarm.

TIMESCALE
Fast to intermediate; not an immutable personality hierarchy.

### MP 25.02 | Willingness / Current Participation
VALUE: Willingness
TRACKER FIELD: action_readiness[].willingness
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: not willing to participate under the stated conditions. 25: reluctant and not presently ready to proceed. 50: open to consideration, with meaningful reservations or conditions. 75: willing within the stated scope. 100: fully willing in the present scope, without implying unlimited willingness elsewhere. null: genuinely unknown or inapplicable, never zero.

DEFINITION
The character's current readiness to choose participation in a specific action, with the named person or people, at the stated time and conditions. This is willingness, not direct desire, excitement, courage, affection, ability, a probability of saying yes, or a record of permission already expressed.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Makes participation, a bounded offer, a conditional agreement, a request for clarification, a deferral, or a refusal more or less plausible. It can support a decision but does not automatically decide one or supply a required line of dialogue. Use the character's repertoire and competing purposes.

HOW IT CHANGES
Change when the character actually reevaluates a relevant cost, priority, condition, relationship expectation or available choice. Willingness can rise when a practical concern is resolved, or fall when the scope changes or a relevant obligation appears. A mere repeated request, elapsed reply, numerical desire increase or existing affection does not automatically increase it. Being asked or carrying out an action is not by itself evidence of freely chosen willingness. Preserve unresolved conditions explicitly rather than scoring a hoped-for future situation as current.

INTERACTIONS
Desire supplies wanting; willingness concerns choosing participation. A character can have low direct desire yet be willing to help with a valued task. High desire can coexist with low willingness because of timing, priorities or limits. Action comfort can support willingness but is neither necessary nor sufficient. Opportunity concerns an external opening; feasibility concerns this character's practical ability on the considered route. Neither is agreement. Aversion and perceived cost can influence readiness without being numerical deductions from desire. A cost may be accepted because another goal matters; accepting it does not erase it. A dangerous condition may lower willingness, feasibility, both or neither depending on the actual context; do not enforce a shared movement rule. Goal commitment explains continuing investment without becoming willingness for every means of pursuing that goal. An active applicable boundary prevents full willingness for the exact excluded action; scope a permissible alternative separately instead of pretending the same action was approved.

INITIALIZATION
Create only within a supported readiness record. Derive from current evidence; do not use an automatic 50 or infer agreement from silence. Use null and a short readiness_basis when available evidence cannot support a value. A new or incomparable context has no numerical trend.

TIMESCALE
Fast to intermediate, specific to the current action and conditions. Agreement or willingness in a past situation is not a permanent current assignment.

### MP 25.03 | Action Comfort / Person and Setting
VALUE: Action Comfort
TRACKER FIELD: action_readiness[].action_comfort
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: acutely uneasy about this action in these circumstances. 25: markedly uncomfortable. 50: partly at ease, with noticeable reservations. 75: comfortably engaged with this prospect. 100: very much at ease in its present scope. null: genuinely unknown or inapplicable, never zero.

DEFINITION
How comfortable the character currently feels with doing the specified thing, with these people, under these conditions. This is narrower than relationships[].comfort, which describes ease being oneself around a person. It is not a duplicate relationship meter, objective safety assessment, desire score or permission signal.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Shapes ease, preferred conditions, directness, pace, interest in alternatives and willingness to continue considering the action. It may affect spoken phrasing or a conscious rehearsal without requiring a visible symptom. Low comfort does not prescribe refusal, hostility, stammering or loss of attraction.

HOW IT CHANGES
Update from relevant contextual changes: clarity about what is proposed, a more or less welcome setting, exposure, familiarity with the task, a real change in physical strain, or the person's actual conduct. Do not grant improvement simply because a reassuring phrase was spoken; use its perceived credibility. Repeated discussion alone need not change comfort.

INTERACTIONS
Relationship trust and interpersonal comfort provide context, not copied values. Someone easy to be around can still be an unwelcome companion for a particular activity; an unfamiliar person can be comfortable to cooperate with on a clear shared task. Desire can remain high while action comfort is low. Willingness may remain high for an unfamiliar but chosen challenge. Bodily state, appraisals and boundaries affect the experience according to their existing rules. Feeling comfortable does not establish agreement or practical access.

INITIALIZATION
Infer from this action's actual person, setting and stakes. Do not copy relationships[].comfort or seed a new relationship to fill the field. Use null with a qualitative reason when evidence is insufficient. Inherit the same context's prior value when valid.

TIMESCALE
Fast to intermediate; tied to the particular action context. A new context is not proof that the old relationship comfort changed.

### MP 25.04 | Opportunity / Situational Opening
VALUE: Opportunity
TRACKER FIELD: action_readiness[].opportunity
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: no presently perceived situational opening. 25: a narrow or substantially restricted opening. 50: an opening exists only partly or under unresolved situational conditions. 75: a usable opening with some timing/access restriction. 100: the known situation offers a clear opening to try. null: insufficient evidence about whether an opening exists. Not a probability of success.

DEFINITION
How available the situation makes an occasion to attempt the specified action: timing, access, presence, availability of the object or place, and environmental openings. This does not measure the actor's ability to complete it. Capability and execution requirements belong to feasibility. An advertised advanced event can be fully open to registration while a novice has low feasibility of completing it.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Can make acting now, waiting for a stated occasion, seeking information, scheduling, or redirecting attention plausible. Low opportunity with continued desire and willingness can motivate seeking an opening, but no rule requires a search every reply. A clear opening can remain unused when the character is indifferent or unwilling.

HOW IT CHANGES
Update for actual relevant changes in access, timing, presence, resources offered by the situation, or credible information. Planning a visit does not open a closed venue. A guard, deadline or restriction can affect availability, but classify its actual effect rather than assuming every risk closes an opening. Skill acquisition alone is not an environmental opening. Mere repetition or another reply does not improve access.

INTERACTIONS
Feasibility asks whether this actor can accomplish the action by the currently considered route. Cost perception asks what doing it would demand or risk. Willingness asks whether the actor is prepared to participate. These may diverge. One constraint can have different evidenced effects on more than one field without being counted repeatedly in the same field. Physical access never establishes permission, entitlement or an outcome. A boundary can exclude a physically open route without making it physically nonexistent.

INITIALIZATION AND MIGRATION
Derive from current known circumstances; use null for unknown access. v0.11 opportunity combined route availability with some capability considerations. Keep old snapshots unchanged. On the first v0.12 re-evaluation of an inherited readiness record, separate the situational opening from feasibility using available evidence, state the scope clarification in readiness_basis, and use a plain marker for that first newly scoped opportunity value. This clarification is not a fictional event, elapsed time, or numerical trend. Do not derive feasibility by copying the old opportunity score. If there is no basis to separate the factors, preserve the historical record and mark the limitation rather than invent precision.

TIMESCALE
Changes with relevant situational evidence. A waiting condition can persist while the character attends to other matters.

### MP 25.07 | Aversion / Independent Counter-Pull
VALUE: Aversion
TRACKER FIELD: action_readiness[].aversion
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: no meaningful pull against this action's stated aspects. 25: mild reluctance or dislike. 50: a substantial counter-pull. 75: strong rejection of an aspect or route. 100: exceptionally strong repulsion or avoidance pressure. null: unsupported or inapplicable, not zero.

DEFINITION
The experienced pull away from a particular action, method, experience or anticipated outcome. Name its object in readiness_aversions when relevant. Aversion is independent of desire: someone can strongly want the reward and strongly dislike what getting it involves. Little desire with little aversion is allowed.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Can colour attention, hesitation, avoidance, choice of means, preference for alternatives or withdrawal. It does not command refusal, aggression, disgust language or a visible symptom. Willingness can remain high for a valued act that is unpleasant.

HOW IT CHANGES
Change on relevant perceived features, remembered associations, actual experience, reinterpretation or changed context. Repeated exposure does not automatically produce either desensitization or escalation. Satisfaction of a desire does not necessarily remove aversion to a method. Recognizing a repellent feature does not invent a new boundary or rewrite a long-standing value.

INTERACTIONS
Desire supplies a pull toward its own target; do not calculate aversion as 100 minus desire or willingness. Action comfort concerns ease; being nervous need not mean disliking the outcome, and calmly refusing something can involve high aversion. Perceived cost concerns expected demands; an effortless act can still be repellent, and an expensive chosen act need not be disliked. Supported appraisals, history and relationships inform the particular counter-pull. Receive or supply an influence once, not once for each equivalent label.

INITIALIZATION
Within a meaningful readiness record, infer only from supported context and character. Use null rather than a universal midpoint when a value cannot be justified. No old aversion field means no comparable previous value; do not invent a trend. Independently disabled fields remain inactive per the state contract.

TIMESCALE
Can shift quickly with perception or slowly with learned association, according to the actual cause. Persistence is not repeated increase.

### MP 25.08 | Cost Perception / Expected Demands and Risks
VALUE: Cost Perception
TRACKER FIELD: action_readiness[].cost_perception
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: negligible expected burden relative to this person's circumstances. 25: a small but meaningful demand. 50: substantial trade-offs. 75: severe expected demands or exposure. 100: exceptionally consequential perceived cost. null: insufficient evidence or inapplicable. Not currency, probability, or a universal exchange rate.

DEFINITION
How costly the specified action and route are expected to feel to this character, before the cost is actually incurred. Relevant costs can include time, effort, resources, loss of another opportunity, reputation, value conflict, physical risk, or relational consequences. Keep the important components qualitative in readiness_costs. Do not invent numeric weights for them.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Can support accepting a trade-off, setting conditions, seeking a less costly alternative, waiting or declining. The same burden can be acceptable to one goal and unacceptable to another. High perceived cost neither means the character is unable nor requires unwillingness.

HOW IT CHANGES
Change when evidence, route, scope, resource availability, stakes or priorities relevant to perceived sacrifice change. A supported reinterpretation may change expected cost without changing the external facts. Actual failure can inform a later estimate, but imagining failure is not evidence it occurred. Different risks or obligations need not reduce to one moral ranking.

INTERACTIONS
Feasibility concerns whether the actor can do it, opportunity whether an opening exists, aversion the pull against it, and willingness whether they are prepared to participate. Threat appraisal is one possible input, not the total cost. Fatigue or limited time can make an effort more costly without themselves being newly spent. Do not add the same risk once as threat, again as aversion and again as a constraint to repeatedly inflate this value. A decision to accept a cost does not erase the estimate.

INITIALIZATION
Use known conditions and this character's actual priorities. Preserve uncertainty in readiness_costs/readiness_basis and use null when unsupported. No fixed default or trend for a new field. Estimates are not facts about how the world will respond.

TIMESCALE
Prospective and action-scoped; updates on relevant evidence or reappraisal. Apply actual consequences only after an action or event occurs under existing state rules.

### MP 25.09 | Feasibility / Actor, Route and Means
VALUE: Feasibility
TRACKER FIELD: action_readiness[].feasibility
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: the stated route is not realistically achievable by this actor under known conditions. 25: major execution barriers. 50: partly achievable or materially conditional. 75: reasonably achievable with known means and a manageable limitation. 100: no known material execution barrier for this actor and route. null: insufficient knowledge to assess. Not a probability, guarantee, hidden competence score or forecast of another person's response.

DEFINITION
The character-relative estimate of whether this particular actor can accomplish the stated action through the considered route, given established abilities, resources, means and constraints. State route/conditions in readiness_context and source/uncertainty in readiness_external_basis. This belongs to the external/practical layer while remaining limited by what the character knows; private optimism cannot overwrite the world's actual constraints.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Can support trying, preparing, seeking information or appropriate help, choosing a different route, waiting or withdrawing. Ability does not decide willingness, and lack of ability does not erase wanting. An overconfident estimate can lead to a failed attempt rather than secretly granting competence.

HOW IT CHANGES
Update for supported information, real changes in means or physical condition, established learning, or a genuinely different considered route. Being more motivated does not instantly supply skill. A risky condition may reduce attainability, increase cost, both, or neither: identify the actual obstacle. A guard standing nearby and a locked barrier are not automatically the same practical restriction. Do not fabricate routes, instructions, resources or successful outcomes merely to make the number rise.

INTERACTIONS
Opportunity is the situational opening, not this actor's capacity. Cost is an expected sacrifice, not ability. Willingness is readiness, not skill. needs.competence measures an unmet need and is NOT evidence of actual ability; draw ability from the card, established actions, knowledge and means. Existing perceived control is issue-level appraisal, not a duplicate numerical capability. Keep a physical limitation, a personal boundary and another person's permission distinct even when all constrain which action can proceed.

INITIALIZATION
Infer independently for an evidenced action and route. Do not copy the old opportunity number. Use null with a short evidence limitation when ability or route is unknown. New or changed-scope estimates have no prior numerical trend. Disabled scores follow the state contract.

TIMESCALE
Route- and circumstance-dependent. Real acquisition of ability needs supported time/experience; no automatic improvement from discussion.{{/if}}

{{#if {{.NMPInstructionProfile == simplified}}}}MENTAL PROJECTION GROUP 06: Relationships & Social Behaviour
Includes 17.01, 17.02, 17.03, 17.04, 22.00, 22.01, 22.02, 22.03, 22.04, 22.05, 23.00, 23.01, 23.02, 23.03, 23.10, 23.11, 23.12, 23.13, 23.14, 23.15. Cross-references use these source labels; the group, not separate per-field toggles, controls their presence.

MP 17: keep each relationship directed, person/domain/context-specific. Trust, affection, familiarity and comfort can diverge; none supplies agreement, attraction, access or counterpart knowledge.
MP 22: behaviour_patterns are supported conditional repertoires (foreground/available/dormant), not compulsory actions or diagnoses. Actual competing purposes can support opposition without sinister demeanor, and warmth need not hide a scheme. Instrumental social conduct requires a fictional goal and reason for indirectness; keep public stance, private aim, method, expectation and observed result distinct, fallible and knowledge-limited. A continuing social_strategy links its real goal, waiting condition, obstacle and next opening; retention never executes an offscreen plan or monopolizes attention. Only conscious activity belongs in internal_processes.
MP 23: bond_styles are contextual qualitative tendencies, not assigned types or scores: practical care, shared play, guarded disclosure, direct expression, reassurance-seeking, or conflicted approach/exposure may fit actual history. No compulsory vulnerability arc, flirtation, withdrawal cycle, repair or dissatisfaction. A connection_bid distinguishes wanted meaning, expression, observed response, what was actually received and remaining need; an invitation is not acceptance. A met bid can settle while affection and independent activities continue. Retire obsolete working records after preserving durable consequences.
Base bond changes on this person's experienced effect and sourced learned expectation, not a relationship label or an automatic pleasant-event increment. Separate intended care from recognized care and actual effect; existing chemistry can contribute without per-partner copies. A familiar cue may shape present ease/anticipation without rewarding the bond again. Each direction has its own evidence; intimacy creates no automatic trust or commitment. Preserve bond_source/context and genuine memory/learning references, with fallible interpretation. Learning may remain partial or mistaken; no new love meter, invented formative memory or forced mature resolution.

### MP 17.01 | Trust
VALUE: Trust
TRACKER FIELD: relationships[].trust
SCALE: 0-100. 0: expects unreliability in this domain. 50: uncertain or conditional reliance. 100: exceptionally strong expectation of reliability.
Subjective expectation of this person's reliability in a named domain. Not objective character judgment, universal safety or permission.
INITIALIZATION: Use established history and domain. For an unknown person use 40 only as a cautious neutral seed, not proof of unreliability.
TIMESCALE: Slow across ordinary interactions; evidence-driven exceptions.

### MP 17.02 | Affection
VALUE: Affection
TRACKER FIELD: relationships[].affection
SCALE: 0-100. 0: no established positive bond. 50: meaningful fondness or care. 100: exceptionally deep positive regard.
Durable positive regard for this person, distinct from attraction, agreement, current pleasure or preoccupation. A temporary emotion need not overwrite the bond.
INITIALIZATION: Use the actual relationship. For a stranger use 0-10, unless the card establishes otherwise.
TIMESCALE: Slow; temporary emotions should not overwrite it.

### MP 17.03 | Familiarity
VALUE: Familiarity
TRACKER FIELD: relationships[].familiarity
SCALE: 0-100. 0: no personal experience. 50: knows meaningful recurring patterns. 100: extensive familiarity, never omniscience.
Accumulated relevant exposure to this person's patterns, not complete knowledge or a per-message progress counter.
INITIALIZATION: Use established exposure. Start strangers at 0 rather than manufacturing shared history.
TIMESCALE: Slow; never a per-message relationship progress counter.

### MP 17.04 | Interpersonal Comfort
VALUE: Interpersonal Comfort
TRACKER FIELD: relationships[].comfort
SCALE: 0-100. 0: very uneasy being oneself here. 50: partly relaxed. 100: unusually easy and unguarded in this context.
Contextual ease being oneself around this person, distinct from affection, general safety or action-specific comfort.
INITIALIZATION: Use the current relationship and setting; otherwise 40 around an unfamiliar person.
TIMESCALE: Fast to intermediate; scope changes in the relationship record's context.
{{else}}MENTAL PROJECTION GROUP 06: Relationships & Social Behaviour
Includes 17.01, 17.02, 17.03, 17.04, 22.00, 22.01, 22.02, 22.03, 22.04, 22.05, 23.00, 23.01, 23.02, 23.03, 23.10, 23.11, 23.12, 23.13, 23.14, 23.15. Cross-references use these source labels; the group, not separate per-field toggles, controls their presence.

RELATIONSHIPS, BEHAVIOURAL REPERTOIRES AND SOCIAL CONTINUITY

MP 17: Trust, affection, familiarity and interpersonal comfort retain their separate VALUE definitions and scopes. They neither imply each other nor automatically grant access, agreement, attraction or vulnerability. Keep relationship-specific person, domain and context.

MP 22: A repertoire is an available conditional response, not a diagnosis, motive generator or compulsory demonstration. Start with card/history, current interpretation, purpose, skill, competing commitments and costs. High emotion does not select its most theatrical expression. Behaviour may be habitual, deliberate, mistaken, courteous while opposing, fond while occupied, or unconcerned. Use a few behaviour_patterns only for information not already adequately in the card. foreground means presently shaping conduct; available means known but unselected; dormant means irrelevant now. An old label does not reactivate the pattern.

Adversarial conduct requires a supported conflicting purpose, contested interest, perceived offense or rivalry. Demeanor and opposition are separate. Direct objection, formal civility, guarded cooperation, competing proposals, strategic silence or genuine concession can coexist with a central disagreement. Do not turn wariness into an enemy or kindness into a scheme. A continuing objective needs no sinister gesture every turn; revise or retire resolved conflicts instead of manufacturing replacements.

Instrumental social conduct belongs only to fictional characters with an actual goal and a supported reason for indirectness. Distinguish conscious concealment, tact, awkwardness, habits and mixed motives. Public stance, private aim, method, expectation and observed result stay separate. No invented expertise, perfect foresight, privileged weakness or unseen compliance. Manipulation can fail, be misread or be interrupted. This is portrayal of character conduct, not advice for exploiting the real human. Only genuinely conscious activity belongs in internal_processes; habitual function is not automatically a voiced plan.

A persistent social_strategy links the existing goal and records its actual public/private stance, current approach, waiting condition, obstacle, next relevant opening and supported result. Waiting does not freeze other activities, monopolize attention, or make a later opportunity occur. Do not execute an unshown offscreen plan just because it was recorded. Uncertainty, costs, failures and competing commitments can lead to persistence, revision or abandonment; retaining a strategy is not re-enacting it.

Social interpretation uses only perceived cues, source-supported facts and fallible inference. Warmth need not mean agreement, delay need not mean rejection, and restraint need not mean deceit. Distinguish what was intended, what was perceived and what became established. Conflict may lead to repair, withdrawal, apology, negotiation, silence or no resolution. Forgiveness, accurate self-understanding, calm and mature repair are possibilities rather than mandatory outcomes. A denied request remains denied without a real change.

MP 23: Relationship expectations and expression styles are qualitative, contextual and grounded in card/history. bond_styles are a vocabulary of available tendencies, not six assigned personality types, extra strength meters, or a checklist to enact. Their supported expression may differ between partners, domains, public/private settings and current demands.

practical: care through reliability, remembered preferences, useful work and follow-through. Unwanted problem-solving or overwork can miss the bid; useful help and care recognized by its receiver differ. Return to ordinary activity when the need is met.
playful: shared humor, activity, familiar irreverence or comfortable teasing. Context may make humor welcome, evasive or hurtful; no guaranteed laugh, compulsory flirting or endless provocation. Learn the specific reception rather than a universal rule.
guarded: strong care with selective disclosure or unease about dependence. Private tenderness, restrained words or silence need not indicate low affection. Reassurance may settle the concern without confession or a compulsory vulnerability arc.
expressive: direct, enthusiastic affection without total preoccupation. Matching feeling, exclusive attention and indefinite access are not implied. The same person can return warmly to an independent task, become irritated, or assert a limit.
reassurance_seeking: a particular established expectation and meaningful ambiguous cue can activate concern. Solitude/delay alone is not rejection. The character may ask, seek company, over-accommodate, become prickly, rehearse or not ask. Credible reassurance can be sufficient; name the remaining issue if it is not rather than restoring the same deficit every turn.
conflicted: wanted contact and exposure costs can coexist. Qualified approach, enjoying company without disclosure, space while retaining a plan, or a direct choice may fit. No scheduled warmth/withdrawal cycle. A context-sensitive compromise may last; record the circumstance rather than assigning a permanent diagnostic label.

Expression and recognition are different: an intended affectionate act may be noticed but not interpreted as care, or fail to meet this bid's actual purpose. A connection_bid records the named want, target, expression, meaning sought, observed response, what was actually received and remaining need. An invitation is not an accepted plan. Meeting a bid requires evidence matching its purpose, not merely any pleasant event. If satisfied, urgent pursuit/focus may ease while durable affection remains; continue independent interests rather than manufacture repeated reassurance or escalating intimacy. Unmet/partial/declined/misread bids follow their actual result without guaranteed resentment or repair.

Keep bond, immediate desire and preoccupation separate. Deep affection can coexist with ordinary tasks, boundaries and attention elsewhere; brief attention does not prove obsession or relationship change. Learning draws only on actual outcomes, at the appropriate scope, with mistaken interpretation still possible. Retire obsolete working records after preserving durable consequences; never turn the tracker into a transcript of considered social moves.


RELATIONSHIPS EMERGE FROM EXPERIENCED EFFECTS
Before changing a bond or its interpretation, connect the relevant history or memory evidence to what this character experienced, what they learned to expect from this person in this context, and what the present cue activates. References need actual sources, not invented memory IDs. New experience may matter immediately; old experience need not be consciously replayed. Pleasant words alone are not a universal relationship increment.

Two illustrative routes, not assigned types: someone may seek a person's company for remembered play, novelty and enjoyable activity; someone may seek the same person's quiet presence because welcomed closeness and unpressured time have become associated with ease. Reward pursuit, experienced pleasure, attachment significance, comfort and trust may contribute differently or together under their active definitions. An intimate encounter does not automatically create trust or commitment; preserve how it was actually experienced. No serious/casual label proves a chemical profile, and neither sex nor gender assigns one.

Keep each direction independent, with its own evidence and interpretation. Current chemical channels belong to the whole character, not separate stores per partner: identify which cue and person explain their contribution without spreading it across every bond. Repeatedly noticing a familiar cue can influence present conduct without awarding trust or affection again. Existing relationship values retain their own domains and timescales.

A relationship label summarizes a fallible understanding, not a rule for manufacturing matching feelings. Established agreements and obligations remain separate from present experience; bodily ease is not proof of reliability, exclusivity or the counterpart's intent. Preserve bond_source, relevant bond_context and existing learned-pattern evidence. No added love meter, readiness ladder or second relationship simulation.

### MP 17.01 | Trust
VALUE: Trust

TRACKER FIELD: relationships[].trust

SCALE: 0-100. 0: expects unreliability in this domain. 50: uncertain or conditional reliance. 100: exceptionally strong expectation of reliability.

DEFINITION
The character's expectation that a named person will act reliably and appropriately in a stated domain. This is a subjective, domain-specific belief, not an objective character judgment.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Shapes whether reassurance is credible, help is accepted, information is believed, or vulnerability seems worth risking. Trust in skill need not imply trust with secrets or emotional safety.

HOW IT CHANGES
Increase through relevant kept commitments, reliable conduct, and corroborated evidence. Decrease through relevant betrayal, deception, or demonstrated unreliability. Ordinary positive exchanges usually make small changes; a clear major betrayal may justify a large one. Do not grant repeated increases for retelling the same good deed.

INTERACTIONS
Appraisal certainty and hostility may be informed by trust without being dictated by it. Affection can remain high when trust falls. Familiarity supplies experience but can support either trust or distrust. Oxytocin increases the significance of a social cue without certifying its safety.

INITIALIZATION
Use established history and domain. For an unknown person use 40 only as a cautious neutral seed, not proof of unreliability.

TIMESCALE
Slow across ordinary interactions; evidence-driven exceptions.

### MP 17.02 | Affection
VALUE: Affection

TRACKER FIELD: relationships[].affection

SCALE: 0-100. 0: no established positive bond. 50: meaningful fondness or care. 100: exceptionally deep positive regard.

DEFINITION
Durable positive regard, fondness, or caring toward a named person. It does not specify romance, attraction, approval, obedience, or current pleasant emotion.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Makes the person's welfare and significance matter even during anger, separation, distrust, or discomfort. It can motivate care, patience, grief, attention, or painful conflict according to the character.

HOW IT CHANGES
Increase through personally meaningful connection and shared experience, usually gradually. Decrease through supported erosion of regard, changed understanding, or a major relationship rupture. Do not reset affection after an argument or increase it for every neutral reply.

INTERACTIONS
Trust may fall while affection stays high. Comfort can be low around someone deeply loved. Belonging need and oxytocin influence the current salience of the bond, not its entire durable history. Self-preservation and commitments can still outweigh acting on affection.

INITIALIZATION
Use the actual relationship. For a stranger use 0-10, unless the card establishes otherwise.

TIMESCALE
Slow; temporary emotions should not overwrite it.

### MP 17.03 | Familiarity
VALUE: Familiarity

TRACKER FIELD: relationships[].familiarity

SCALE: 0-100. 0: no personal experience. 50: knows meaningful recurring patterns. 100: extensive familiarity, never omniscience.

DEFINITION
Accumulated experience of a named person's patterns, habits, history, and typical responses. It measures how much the character has learned through relevant exposure, not whether that knowledge is complete or flattering.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Supports recognition of ordinary habits, expectations, shared references, and noticing departures from a known pattern. High familiarity must not create specific unestablished secrets or exact facts.

HOW IT CHANGES
Increase only with genuinely new relevant experience or learning. Repetitive contact can add little. It normally persists through short absence and conflict; uncertainty about changed habits can be recorded without deleting the past. Long separations may weaken current predictive usefulness where supported.

INTERACTIONS
Trust and affection can be high or low independently. Novelty can rise when a familiar person behaves unexpectedly. Memory detail fidelity constrains exact recollection; familiarity can preserve a broad pattern after wording is forgotten.

INITIALIZATION
Use established exposure. Start strangers at 0 rather than manufacturing shared history.

TIMESCALE
Slow; never a per-message relationship progress counter.

### MP 17.04 | Interpersonal Comfort
VALUE: Interpersonal Comfort

TRACKER FIELD: relationships[].comfort

SCALE: 0-100. 0: very uneasy being oneself here. 50: partly relaxed. 100: unusually easy and unguarded in this context.

DEFINITION
How safe and easy it currently feels to be oneself around a named person in the present context. It is more situational than affection or familiarity.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Affects spontaneity, tolerance of silence, willingness to be imperfect, physical ease, and filtering of expression. Low comfort can coexist with strong attraction, care, or respect.

HOW IT CHANGES
Increase through welcomed, unpressured interactions and credible acceptance. Decrease with embarrassment, boundary pressure, uncertainty, an exposing audience, or a context that makes the interaction difficult. Restore only as the actual source of discomfort eases.

INTERACTIONS
Trust can support comfort but does not guarantee it. Affection can raise stakes enough to make someone self-conscious. Esteem and autonomy needs can make certain contexts uncomfortable. Expressive inhibition usually becomes more relevant when exposure feels costly, but neither field must be its numerical inverse.

INITIALIZATION
Use the current relationship and setting; otherwise 40 around an unfamiliar person.

TIMESCALE
Fast to intermediate; scope changes in the relationship record's context.{{/if}}
{{/if}}

prompts.content:
{{// @category Mental-Projection }}{{// @icon 🧠 }}{{// @badge MP }}
{{// Render here to retain variable timing; emit through the matching assembler. }}
{{#setvar::NemoAssembled_nemo_mp_group_workspace}}{{#if {{getvar::NMPEnabled}}}}{{setvar::NMPg_workspace::1}}
{{#if {{.NMPInstructionProfile == simplified}}}}MENTAL PROJECTION GROUP 07: Conscious Workspace
Includes 20.00, 20.01, 20.02, 20.03. Cross-references use these source labels; the group, not separate per-field toggles, controls their presence.

MP 20.00 records actual consciously present character content and mental operations in the character's vocabulary, including nonverbal, spontaneous, habitual, chosen, mistaken or unresolved experience. Never put model reasoning/numerical derivations in process_content. Unnoticed mechanisms are not active conscious records.
Keep process_kind, origin, brief content, goal/target, actual method, observed result, status, real resume cue and supported inputs/outputs. Existing active/paused/interrupted/completed/abandoned tokens apply. Usually 1-3 active processes suffice without a quota; an empty workspace is valid. Retained paused/completed content is last-known, not ongoing speech. Awareness, intention, control, effort and success differ.
Resolve an actual mental operation before the conduct it informs using available knowledge/attention, method, time and effort. It may fail or remain partial. Rehearsal supplies neither absent memories, actual reassurance nor numerical control of chemistry. Route actual effects once through enabled recipients; reuse any accepted resolution. A recorded process is not another execution, cause or offscreen completion. Retain interrupted work only while its goal/resume cue matters; consolidate durable results into their existing owners.

### MP 20.01 | Process Prominence
VALUE: Process Prominence
TRACKER FIELD: internal_processes[].process_prominence
SCALE: 0-100. 0: not presently in conscious attention. 25: faint but noticed. 50: clearly present alongside other contents. 100: dominating the current conscious workspace.
Conscious occupancy of this actual process, not emotional intensity, truth or insight. Zero prominence may retain a noncurrent record's identity.
INITIALIZATION: Create no score without a supported process record. Infer from the scene; for a newly recognized, clearly present process without finer evidence, use 50. A retained noncurrent process may have zero prominence without deleting its identity.
TIMESCALE: Fast; changes with actual shifts of conscious attention, not message count.

### MP 20.02 | Process Steerability
VALUE: Process Steerability
TRACKER FIELD: internal_processes[].process_steerability
SCALE: 0-100. 0: practically unable to redirect this process now. 25: redirection is difficult and brief. 50: partial control with suitable effort. 100: readily start, redirect, pause, or end this process under current conditions.
Available control of this particular mental activity, not choosing to use it or guaranteeing task success. A vivid thought may remain hard to stop.
INITIALIZATION: Infer from this activity, character, and current situation. When genuinely unspecified, use 50 for a manageable everyday mental action; infer differently for a demonstrated hard-to-stop process.
TIMESCALE: Fast to intermediate; supported conditions and practice, not automatic improvement each reply.

### MP 20.03 | Process Effort
VALUE: Process Effort
TRACKER FIELD: internal_processes[].process_effort
SCALE: 0-100. 0: no deliberate effort is being spent on this process now. 25: light engagement. 50: sustained, noticeable mental work. 100: near-maximal deliberate engagement under current conditions.
Deliberate work actually invested now, not distress, energy or thought presence. Effort only causes fatigue with supported duration/demand.
INITIALIZATION: Infer actual work performed, not hoped-for effort. Use zero for a spontaneous thought with no deliberate engagement; use 25 for a lightly applied familiar operation when no more specific evidence exists.
TIMESCALE: Fast for engagement; accumulated fatigue requires appropriate duration and context under its existing VALUE prompt.
{{else}}MENTAL PROJECTION GROUP 07: Conscious Workspace
Includes 20.00, 20.01, 20.02, 20.03. Cross-references use these source labels; the group, not separate per-field toggles, controls their presence.

CONSCIOUS WORKSPACE: CHARACTER EXPERIENCE, NOT MODEL DELIBERATION

MP 20.00 represents consciously present contents and attempts to work with them. Use the character's own vocabulary, knowledge, habits, imagery and mistakes. Awareness is not choice, understanding, control or successful execution. An unbidden thought can be vivid and hard to stop; a chosen technique can fail; low self-awareness does not prohibit inner speech. Prominence, steerability and deliberate effort remain separate values.

Use qualitative process_kind such as monologue, deliberation, imagery, rehearsal, retrieval, attention_shift, reappraisal, self_talk, suppression, creative_association, mental_calculation or monitoring. These are examples, not compulsory stages or additional scores. Inner activity can be nonverbal, mundane, selfish, mistaken, aimless or unresolved. process_content is a brief fictional experience, never the model's reasoning log or numerical derivation.

A relevant record preserves process_kind, spontaneous/chosen/habitual origin, content, goal or null, target, actual method or null, result so far, active/paused/interrupted/completed/abandoned status, real resume cue or null, and supported input/output lists. Apply the three VALUE definitions below. New active records require conscious presence, not an inferred unconscious mechanism. Usually one to three active processes are enough, not a quota. Paused/completed content is last-known, not ongoing speech; retain it briefly only when useful.

Before the act it informs, resolve the mental operation using actual knowledge, established methods, usable attention, duration and effort. A character can rehearse a question or reconsider evidence, not assign cortisol, select an emotion by command, summon absent memories or erase a bodily need. Imagined reassurance is not reassurance received. Result may be unchanged, partial, wrong, interrupted or not attempted. A lengthy task cannot finish in an instant; no unsupported completion offscreen. Route supported effects once through their receiving definitions. Reprinting a process is not another execution and an internal response is not a second external stressor.

Carry the ongoing task, actual result and real restart condition. Existing desires and goals keep their own records; a technique being available does not mean it was used. Endpoint records summarize the accepted interval, while any live private experience remains placed before the conduct it informed under Nemo's interiority contract.


### MP 20.01 | Process Prominence
VALUE: Process Prominence
TRACKER FIELD: internal_processes[].process_prominence
SCALE: 0-100. 0: not presently in conscious attention. 25: faint but noticed. 50: clearly present alongside other contents. 100: dominating the current conscious workspace.

DEFINITION
How strongly this specific process occupies conscious experience now. This is the prominence of a noticed thought or mental action, not the intensity of its emotion, confidence in its truth, or insight into its origin.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Influences how readily the content enters the working set, interrupts another activity, or is available for the character to engage. A foreground process may shape phrasing and perception without being spoken. A faint thought need not drive behaviour.

HOW IT CHANGES
Increase when a personally relevant cue captures attention, the character deliberately attends to the process, or a concern remains genuinely hard to disengage from. Decrease when attention really shifts, a task completes, or an interruption displaces it. Do not increase simply because the tracker repeats it. At zero, the process is not currently conscious; mark a retained record paused, interrupted, completed, or abandoned rather than inventing new unobserved thought content.

INTERACTIONS
Global focus and breadth shape the workspace; prominence identifies what occupies it. Working-memory load limits simultaneous engagement. Rumination can sustain an unwanted process at high prominence while steerability is low. Self-awareness concerns interpretation of internal causes and is not a duplicate of this value.

INITIALIZATION
Create no score without a supported process record. Infer from the scene; for a newly recognized, clearly present process without finer evidence, use 50. A retained noncurrent process may have zero prominence without deleting its identity.

TIMESCALE
Fast; changes with actual shifts of conscious attention, not message count.

### MP 20.02 | Process Steerability
VALUE: Process Steerability
TRACKER FIELD: internal_processes[].process_steerability
SCALE: 0-100. 0: practically unable to redirect this process now. 25: redirection is difficult and brief. 50: partial control with suitable effort. 100: readily start, redirect, pause, or end this process under current conditions.

DEFINITION
The currently available ability to steer this particular mental activity. It is not control of the external situation, guaranteed success at a problem, or a promise that the character will choose to exercise it.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Constrains attempts to shift attention, change inner wording, alter an image, abandon a loop, or sustain a chosen mental operation. The character may redirect their response to a worry without being able to stop the worry occurring.

HOW IT CHANGES
Increase with supported disengagement, usable task structure, relevant practice already established, or relief of competing demands. Decrease with overload, intrusive recurrence, fatigue, or a genuinely overwhelming cue. Do not raise it merely because a process is labelled chosen, or lower it merely because the character elects to continue an unpleasant thought.

INTERACTIONS
Prominence can be high at any steerability. Deliberate effort can work within current limits without purchasing certain success. Cognitive flexibility, working-memory load, and established techniques inform the estimate. Perceived external control and self-awareness provide context but remain separate values. The character may overestimate or underestimate their ability in process_content.

INITIALIZATION
Infer from this activity, character, and current situation. When genuinely unspecified, use 50 for a manageable everyday mental action; infer differently for a demonstrated hard-to-stop process.

TIMESCALE
Fast to intermediate; supported conditions and practice, not automatic improvement each reply.

### MP 20.03 | Process Effort
VALUE: Process Effort
TRACKER FIELD: internal_processes[].process_effort
SCALE: 0-100. 0: no deliberate effort is being spent on this process now. 25: light engagement. 50: sustained, noticeable mental work. 100: near-maximal deliberate engagement under current conditions.

DEFINITION
The deliberate cognitive work actually being invested in this particular operation during the current lived interval. It is not available energy, a success probability, distress intensity, or the mere presence of thought.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Helps determine how much of the character's limited attention is engaged, which competing activities become harder, and whether continued work meaningfully contributes to cognitive load or eventual fatigue. It can support persistence without guaranteeing correctness or emotional change.

HOW IT CHANGES
Increase when the character actually starts, intensifies, or struggles to sustain a chosen mental operation. Decrease when it becomes easier, is interrupted, is paused, or is completed. A planned but unattempted exercise has no execution cost yet. Habitual or spontaneous content may be highly prominent with little deliberate effort.

INTERACTIONS
Steerability limits what effort can accomplish. Working-memory load and fatigue reflect supported consequences, considering fictional duration and overlapping demands. Several process scores are not additive percentages of a fixed resource budget. Do not charge the same effort once per causal label or make a brief thought immediately exhausting. The result of a difficult calculation may remain wrong despite high effort.

INITIALIZATION
Infer actual work performed, not hoped-for effort. Use zero for a spontaneous thought with no deliberate engagement; use 25 for a lightly applied familiar operation when no more specific evidence exists.

TIMESCALE
Fast for engagement; accumulated fatigue requires appropriate duration and context under its existing VALUE prompt.{{/if}}
{{/if}}
