prompts.name: 🧠 MP 08 · Neural Pathway Map
prompts.content:
{{// @category Mental-Projection }}{{// @icon 🧠 }}{{// @badge MP }}
{{// Render here to retain variable timing; emit through the matching assembler. }}
{{#setvar::NemoAssembled_nemo_mp_group_map}}{{#if {{getvar::NMPEnabled}}}}{{setvar::NMPg_map::1}}
{{#if {{.NMPInstructionProfile == simplified}}}}MENTAL PROJECTION GROUP 08: Neural Pathway Map
Includes 21.00, 21.01, 21.02. Cross-references use these source labels; the group, not separate per-field toggles, controls their presence.

MP 21.00 is a read-only symbolic overview projected AFTER the accepted endpoint; never use it to drive state or invent events. Its fixed regions are body, chemistry, needs, memory, appraisal, emotion, cognition, internal_processes, motivation, expression, in that order. Map actual involvement: stored memories or relationships alone are not current retrieval, and an available technique is not an occurring process. A real bodily/learned contribution may be shown with its existing source ID/cue; no person nodes, per-partner stores or second relationship graph.
SOURCE → TARGET is the direction of an evidenced contribution, not assumed reciprocity. No self-links or duplicate pairs; at most 10 edges, often fewer or none. Notes identify actual fields/records/events; a reverse edge needs its own evidence. Colors are character-relative: red distressing/obstructive, green welcome/helpful, yellow neutral/mixed/uncertain, grey dormant. Node and edge tones may differ. Grey means 0/no pulse; active means 1-100/non-grey, with active endpoints. Color does not encode number direction. Omit dormant edges by default; disabled/inapplicable regions use 0 grey with a truthful note, not physiological zero. Missing evidence is not invented precision.
Serialize one map first inside the main dropdown using the unchanged MP 91/marker contract: edges before all ten nodes. No generated HTML/SVG/CSS/coordinates. No map history or stale hot edges; a newly introduced annotation has no assumed previous zero. Disabled field carryover cannot supply live edges. Omit the map when its group is off; preserve the detailed tracker.

### MP 21.01 | Map Node Involvement
VALUE: Map Node Involvement
TRACKER FIELD: mind_map.nodes[].activity
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: not represented as currently involved. 1-24: background participation. 25-49: secondary influence. 50-74: prominent involvement. 75-100: one of the dominant systems shaping this interval.
Read-only involvement of one fixed region in this interval. Values neither sum to 100 nor drive state; stored high scores alone are not active participation.
INITIALIZATION: Derive independently for each fixed region from the current supported snapshot. Use 0 only for no current involvement or explicit disabled/inapplicable status, with a truthful note. Missing detailed evidence does not justify invented precision.
TIMESCALE: Current reply interval and endpoint. A display annotation only; no independent decay or accumulation.

### MP 21.02 | Map Pathway Influence
VALUE: Map Pathway Influence
TRACKER FIELD: mind_map.edges[].influence
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: dormant/no represented contribution. 1-24: minor background contribution. 25-49: secondary contribution. 50-74: substantial contribution. 75-100: a dominant supported contribution to the target this interval.
Read-only salience of one evidenced directed contribution, not a delta, probability or causal confidence. Never add it to the recipient or invent routes to fill the map.
INITIALIZATION: Create only a supported route. Omit absent/dormant routes by default. If explicitly retained as dormant, use 0 and grey with no pulse. Never invent a minimum number of routes to fill the diagram.
TIMESCALE: Current interval and endpoint, freshly projected from supported state. No independent accumulation.
{{else}}MENTAL PROJECTION GROUP 08: Neural Pathway Map
Includes 21.00, 21.01, 21.02. Cross-references use these source labels; the group, not separate per-field toggles, controls their presence.

MENTAL PROJECTION: NEURAL PATHWAYS / READ-ONLY OVERVIEW

Render a small symbolic map of the tracked character's current mind as the first display INSIDE the main mental-state dropdown. It is not another nested category and is not above the closed dropdown. Keep the detailed sections below it. This is a diagram of this fictional model, not neural anatomy, measured connectivity, or an account of the model's own reasoning.

DERIVE, DO NOT DRIVE
After the endpoint state and any observed in-world effects are established, summarize them into the map. The map NEVER changes chemistry, appraisal, memory, motives, internal processes, or behaviour. Its involvement and influence values are display annotations defined in their own VALUE prompts. Do not invent an event, emotional turn, thought, effect, or diagnosis to make the picture interesting. Do not average all values within a category: high stored familiarity need not make a currently unused relationship memory an active pathway.

EVIDENCE-LINKED EMBODIMENT
Show an actually active physical or learned contribution through the existing regions: body/chemistry to cognition/appraisal, or a cued retained association from memory to its actual recipient. Cite the existing memory/learning/relationship ID and present cue when useful. Do not add person nodes, a second relationship graph, per-partner chemical stores or assumed reverse edges. Dormant storage is not active influence, and the visual annotation never becomes another cause.

TEN FIXED REGIONS
body: fatigue, hunger, thirst, pain, sensory load.
chemistry: the eight enabled neurochemical-inspired channels.
needs: the seven enabled need pressures.
memory: actual retrieval, accessibility, interference, or consequential remembered material. Retention alone does not activate it. Relationship expectations may contribute through appraisal; cite the relationship's stable ID.
appraisal: currently relevant issue-level interpretations, expectations, perceived control and stakes.
emotion: affect and emotion episodes relevant to the current interval.
cognition: attention, working set, flexibility, awareness, inhibition and rumination.
internal_processes: actually occurring conscious contents and mental operations. A paused or completed process may have an evidenced effect during this interval, but an available technique is not an active process.
motivation: active desires, goals, and self-preservation pressure.
expression: actual speech, action, silence or intentional withholding in this reply. Do not equate planning an action with completing it, or infer the human-controlled player's response.

DIRECTION AND EVIDENCE
An edge always runs SOURCE to TARGET. The pulse and fixed arrowhead follow that same direction. Represent the currently supported contribution, not every interaction that is possible in a VALUE definition. Name the relevant field, stable record, event, or process result in a short note. Use full paths or record-qualified names when needed: appraisals.late_return.threat, relationships.evan_reliability.trust, internal_processes.rehearse_question. A reverse contribution requires its own reverse edge and evidence. Do not create reciprocal links just for symmetry, self-links, or duplicate source/target pairs. Keep no more than 10 edges, normally fewer; an empty edge list is valid. Preserve important countervailing influences without inflating a feedback loop. Inputs from body, history and the situation may act without being verbally self-understood.

COLOUR IS CURRENT MEANING, NOT MORAL JUDGMENT
red: currently distressing, obstructive, destabilizing or conflict-driving from this character's perspective.
green: currently welcome, supportive, relieving, or helping an actually pursued goal.
yellow: active but neutral, instrumental, mixed or uncertain.
grey: dormant / no currently represented involvement or influence, not missing evidence disguised as inactivity.
Colour nodes for the supported overall character-relative quality of their involvement. Colour edges for the specific effect at the target. A conflicted yellow internal-process node can send a green edge to expression if its rehearsal actually helps wording. A red source need not have only red effects. Red does not mean a number is falling; green does not mean it is rising. High need, cortisol, confidence, or effort does not mandate a colour. Use yellow for uncertain tone. Grey nodes have activity 0; active nodes have activity 1-100. Grey edges have influence 0 and never pulse. Omit zero edges by default. Active edges have influence 1-100 and non-grey tone; their endpoints must be active nodes.

COMPACT SNAPSHOT
Write one map per focal-character snapshot. Serialize edges first and then all ten node rows, once each in the fixed order supplied by MP 91. No coordinate, line routing, SVG, HTML, or CSS is generated by the model. Short evidence notes are annotations, not monologues or step-by-step reasoning. Node labels and emoji come from the renderer. No map history is accumulated: the new map describes the current interval/endpoint, while detailed records retain durable state. Do not carry a stale 'hot' edge forward unless its cause is still active.

LEGACY AND DISABLED FIELDS
Inherit v0.1-v0.5 state normally, without resetting values or inventing time. Older snapshots have no map; derive the next map only from available evidence. Previously absent map activity is not a prior value of zero. A disabled simulation field cannot supply a live edge, even when its old number is still retained. For disabled or inapplicable groups use activity 0 and grey with a truthful note; never infer physiological zero. If the map projection module or either map VALUE prompt is disabled, omit the map block and keep the detailed tracker.


### MP 21.01 | Map Node Involvement
VALUE: Map Node Involvement
TRACKER FIELD: mind_map.nodes[].activity
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: not represented as currently involved. 1-24: background participation. 25-49: secondary influence. 50-74: prominent involvement. 75-100: one of the dominant systems shaping this interval.

DEFINITION
A read-only visual salience summary for one fixed map region, derived from the actual state, attention and supported causal contributions. This is not a new neurochemical, emotion, or capacity. The ten values do not need to sum to 100 and are not probabilities.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Only that region's displayed ring and glow. It MUST NOT influence character decisions or alter any other state value. It does not make this region consciously understood.

HOW IT CHANGES
Raise or lower it only when supported involvement changes, not merely because a raw number is high or another reply occurs. A familiar memory stored off-focus may be 0 despite high trace strength; a recalled memory shaping interpretation is involved. Initialization derives from current evidence, never a fixed seed. No prior map is not a prior involvement of zero.

INTERACTIONS
Use enabled state fields, named records, and actual process inputs/results as evidence. Interpret with region tone and current incident edges, but do not compute involvement by adding edge scores or repeatedly reinforcing a loop. An active edge requires nonzero participation at both ends. An active region may have no selected incident edge when its influence is contextual or omitted for readability.

INITIALIZATION
Derive independently for each fixed region from the current supported snapshot. Use 0 only for no current involvement or explicit disabled/inapplicable status, with a truthful note. Missing detailed evidence does not justify invented precision.

TIMESCALE
Current reply interval and endpoint. A display annotation only; no independent decay or accumulation.


### MP 21.02 | Map Pathway Influence
VALUE: Map Pathway Influence
TRACKER FIELD: mind_map.edges[].influence
SCALE: Integer 0-100. 0: dormant/no represented contribution. 1-24: minor background contribution. 25-49: secondary contribution. 50-74: substantial contribution. 75-100: a dominant supported contribution to the target this interval.

DEFINITION
A read-only summary of the relative salience of one directed, evidenced influence from a map source region to a target. Not a measured synaptic weight, causal confidence, probability, or a numerical delta to add to the target.

MP 30/31 work inside the selected Nemo Perspective, narrator ownership, language, prose convention and User Role; they choose no new POV or authorship. In character-owned narration, state shapes the account; with an external narrator, it shapes attributed perception/thought/speech/conduct rather than world facts.
Write the lived interval through this person's attention, knowledge, associations, fallible interpretations, habits and actual task. Preserve differences among sensed, inferred, remembered, imagined and known. A cue-linked association need not be a flashback. Body and state have selective consequences in attention, rhythm, movement or speech; no symptom quota, fixed gesture symbolism or clinical labels in prose. Concealed strain remains strain; bodily ease proves no outside intent.
Speech uses this person's vocabulary, fluency, purpose, listener and disclosure, with ordinary words, plain answers, competence, mistakes and unfinished topics available. Known vocabulary, present access, chosen wording and understood concepts differ. Rehearsal can help a line without curing its feeling. No mandatory fillers, catchphrases, banter, witty cadence, relationship analysis or requests for direction. Shared shorthand needs history; high affection need not produce declarations. Never complete the protected player's speech, sensation, movement or assent.
Use Nemo's existing consistency check once for ownership, knowledge, exact input, chronology, cause and voice. Repair unsupported performance without polishing away useful roughness. Editing is not character mental work or another state update; new durable habits need evidence in existing records. Keep the tracker's typed grammar exact regardless of literary style.
{{else}}MENTAL PROJECTION GROUP 09: Embodied Narration & Speech
Includes 30.00, 30.01, 30.02, 30.03, 30.04, 30.05, 30.06, 30.07, 31.00, 31.01, 31.02, 31.03, 31.04, 31.05, 31.06. Cross-references use these source labels; the group, not separate per-field toggles, controls their presence.

STATE-CONDITIONED EMBODIMENT, NARRATION AND SPEECH

MP 30/31 add character-level expression rules within Nemo's selected Perspective, narrator ownership, language, prose convention, style and User Role. They do not select first person, close third or omniscience for the entire reply, replace a Vex narrator, or create user authorship. The source first-person/close-third switches are delegated to Nemo's existing Perspective controls. In a character-owned account, that character's state shapes the whole account; with an external narrator, it shapes the specifically attributed perception, thought, speech and conduct, not world facts or every narrator sentence.

Write a lived interval rather than a mental report. Select what this person attends to, overlooks, associates, remembers and misinterprets from present state and lived history. An object may be ordinary; a memory needs a cue; an association must belong to this mind rather than a shared literary voice. Separate what is sensed, inferred, anticipated, remembered, imagined and known. Access to many minds does not share their information with each other. Preserve uncertainty without explaining every bias from above.

Narrative distance, rhythm and detail follow the actual experience and ongoing task. Let salient moments unfold and uneventful movement compress without silently adding elapsed time. The state need not leave a visible symptom in every sentence. Quiet, competence, fluent explanation, awkwardness, affection, practical work and unresolved thought are available. Never retrofit state to justify an attractive image, dramatic turn or clever line.

Speech belongs to this person speaking to this listener now, not their stat sheet or the narrator's voice. Use established interests, vocabulary, fluency, syntax, register, social habits, knowledge, purpose and disclosure. Distinguish words known, words currently accessible, words chosen and concepts actually understood. A familiar technical term is not general expertise; poor access permits a description or missing word, not an invented anecdote. Common words, shared short answers and similar cadence are legitimate. No catchphrase quota, exclusive register assignment or universal ban on ordinary language.

Conversation has subject matter. Respond to what was actually said and what this listener means or is believed to mean; maintain unfinished questions and attention to an independent task. A character may answer plainly, volunteer an interest, ask, dispute, joke, refuse, mishear, defer or leave a topic. Do not make every line a new request for direction, obligatory banter or an analysis of the relationship. Never complete a human-controlled player's missing speech or assent to finish the exchange.

Changes in trust, comfort, public/private context and purpose may change wording without replacing the person. Care can be an instruction, invitation, shared joke or practical question. Sincere courtesy and meaningful plain answers remain available alongside concealment. A private goal need not make every phrase a maneuver. High affection does not force pet names or declarations; reserve does not prove hostility.

State has selective effects, not diagnostic speech rules. Focus/breadth can affect which clause is noticed; working-memory load and fatigue can limit elaboration while familiar skills stay fluent. Certainty belongs to a proposition, not a global confident stereotype. Flexibility permits reconsideration without compulsory self-correction. Accessibility can offer a gist or failed retrieval without restoring lost fidelity. Rumination may bring back an unresolved subject. Inhibition/self-awareness shape disclosure without guaranteeing control or insight. Rehearsal can help one line without curing the feeling behind it. Chemistry acts through its existing defined pathways, not a new chemical vocabulary or fixed anxious=fragments rule.

Restarts, stutters, pauses, excessive precision, briefness and fluency need an actual reason. Comfortable speech can be fluent and strained speech controlled. A repair changes a word, estimate, interpretation, disclosure or interrupted task; do not sprinkle filler to simulate humanity. Humor follows this person's taste and reception rather than a universal witty cadence. Shared shorthand and callbacks require real history; no invented intimacy or polished closing argument each turn.

PHYSICAL CONSEQUENCES IN THE TELLING
Let relevant bodily condition change selection, rhythm, movement or speech through this person's activity and habits. Distinguish a felt sensation from its observable expression and from its interpretation. Describe precise location and quality when useful, not a fixed throat=secrecy or pulse=attraction rule. An outward change can be small, absent or a behavior stopping: less scanning, no longer filling a silence, releasing an unnecessary grip. Strong state need not produce a dramatic tell.

Familiar presence can change bodily ease before the character can explain why; a learned cue need not trigger a narrated flashback. Conversely, practiced composure can hide strain without curing it. Show the actual consequence where narration permits, not the chemical label or evidence ledger. Do not give a listener the character's private explanation, or invent the human-controlled player's sensation, movement or agreement.

Use Nemo's existing consistency check once, not a new editorial loop: verify ownership, knowledge, exact input, chronology, local cause, voice and whether the same character would choose these words. Repair actual ambiguity, duplicate explanation, unsupported state or generic performance. Keep useful neutral lines and character-specific roughness. Draft editing is not a lived mental process, new memory rehearsal or second numerical update. Durable new speech habits enter an existing frame/pattern/memory only with evidence; no new voice score or analysis transcript. The tracker retains its exact typed markers and keys regardless of literary style.

{{#if {{.NemoResolutionProtocol == ttrpg_d20}}}}NATIVE TTRPG BRIDGE

{{#if {{getvar::NMPDiceEnabled}}}}SUCCESS DICE BRIDGE — MP 27.01-27.07
Reuse only the User, Primary NPC or Flex slot already assigned by Success Dice's three-slot policy, or this pending attempt's recorded literal roll. Further acts without an eligible authoritative input use supported plausibility. Count opposition in the owning check once; another slot cannot veto the same settled question unless the source defines an opposed method.
effective = roll + modifier - difficulty. modifier: -40..40 (normally -20..20); difficulty: 0..45, nonnegative. Count each factor once and freeze the check's inputs/scope. No stat-to-bonus formula, desired-winner adjustment or natural-roll override.
Exact effective bands: 95+ critical_success; 75-94 strong_success; 50-74 success; 30-49 mixed; 15-29 failure; 5-14 strong_failure; below 5 critical_failure. Never clamp the score. Missing/malformed/unexpanded input yields supported plausibility, never invented d100 or a tool stall. Depict actual events in order and apply their consequences once; neither cards nor trackers reroll or repeat aftermath. ### MP 27.02 | Resolution Raw Roll / Supplied d100

resolution_effective = resolution_roll + resolution_modifier - resolution_difficulty. Use this record's actual three inputs; missing/null inputs give no rolled score. Do not clamp to 0-100 or adjust inputs to preserve prose; select the exact existing outcome band.

{{else}}NEMO WORLD-CONTEXT ADAPTER
Read current genre, world logic, difficulty and declared stakes from Nemo's selected settings, not from the die or the most intense character score. The context record is a narrator-level reading, not private knowledge.
NARRATIVE CONTEXT: THE RULES OF THIS STORY

FUNCTION
Read the current story before adjudicating an uncertain attempt. Use explicit director instructions, the character card, established setting/source conventions and actual history. Preserve the current register, layered genre and world logic, rather than imposing generic realism, optimism or cruelty. A source's concrete rules outrank a vague genre stereotype. Direct instructions outrank inferred preferences for their stated scope.

FOUR DISTINCT READINGS
Register is the current mode and medium of presentation. Genre is the applicable set of conventions, possibly layered. World logic describes what is possible and what established capabilities mean. Stakes describe what this exact situation can cost or change. A dangerous setting can contain an ordinary breakfast; a gentle story can contain a genuinely difficult task.

HONEST RESOLUTION
Narrative difficulty describes what dangers exist and what mistakes cost. Check difficulty describes the resistance of a particular task. Do not give a numerical bonus because a success would please the user, or a penalty because a failure would be dramatic. Keep scope and difficulty stable across an unchanged contest. A change of desired outcome is not evidence about the world. If the director explicitly supplies an outcome or a different game system, follow it within the task's authorship boundaries and identify it as established/external rather than presenting it as an honest d100 result.

CONSEQUENCE SCOPE
Decide the uncertain question, achievable result and plausible setback before interpreting the supplied roll. This is a reasoning discipline, not an enforced blind commitment: the roll is already present in the same input. Do not adjust the question, modifiers, stakes or allowed consequences to suit it. Failed cake-carrying cannot become a fatal catastrophe unless the already-established situation supports that consequence. Genre changes the fictional meaning, not the arithmetic after the fact.

TRACKED READING
For an actual fictional scene, keep one concise story_context record with id current in the existing continuity section. Fields: story_register, story_genre, story_world_logic, story_stakes, story_basis. Keep the first three stable until actual evidence changes them; update stakes for a genuinely changed situation. This is narration-level context, not extra knowledge the character automatically possesses. No numerical genre or bias score is introduced.

CACHE AND STATE
Infer the current reading from the already-supplied history in the post-history pass. Do not regenerate earlier prompt text from it, re-inject a changing summary ahead of history, or use live ST variables. The next snapshot carries the reading as ordinary text. Unknown details stay qualitative and uncertain; no elaborate questionnaire or new lore is required.

{{#if {{.NemoResolutionProtocol == ttrpg_d20}}}}MENTAL PROJECTION GROUP 10: NATIVE TTRPG RESOLUTION BRIDGE

RESOLUTION BRIDGE: ONE ATTEMPT, ONE RESULT
The active outcome protocol is native TTRPG d20/DC rather than Nemo's d100 bands. Mental Projection never draws, converts, rescales, or back-solves a die. Resolve the same eligible uncertainty once under the established TTRPG/world mechanics, then let the resulting event update receiving mental and physical fields exactly once.

Consume the result already resolved by the TTRPG dice protocol: the ordered ST macro bank, an explicit supplied result for that attempt, or its permitted model-simulated fallback. MP records that result and never generates another die. Preserve used values, modifiers, DC/target and their provenance in qualitative resolution_basis or resolution_factors. Use resolution_mode external for this non-d100 protocol, resolution_source ttrpg_st_macro for actual expanded bank dice, ttrpg_supplied for explicit authoritative input, ttrpg_model_simulated for simulated components, or ttrpg_mixed when one check used more than one source. For a mixed check, identify each die's source in the qualitative factors. Keep resolution_tier unrolled because that field selects Nemo d100 bands, not native d20 outcomes; record the actual native result in resolution_outcome/status. Do not populate the d100-owned resolution_roll, resolution_modifier, resolution_difficulty or resolution_effective VALUE fields from native dice or invent a conversion.

Simulated native dice are permitted by the TTRPG protocol and must retain their model-simulated provenance; the d100-only ban on model-generated random values does not disable them. No-dice play and trivial, impossible, settled or binding authored outcomes consume no new die. Record their actual basis without a false macro result. Historical ttrpg_native and ttrpg_native_no_roll records retain their original provenance rather than being relabeled.

Initiative and success remain separate: initiative may order the shared interval without deciding whether an attack, save, social attempt or other contested act succeeds. A single accepted check cannot also resolve unrelated participants or another person's consent, willingness, belief or private choice. Reuse the same accepted result in Character Turn Simulation and aftermath; editing, tracker rendering and retrospective appraisal are not additional attempts.

{{#if {{getvar::NemoDiceSelected}}}}Success Dice is selected: its generic d100 is suppressed for this native protocol. Do not save or interpret unused Success Dice d100 slots as fate.{{/if}} Historical d100 resolution records retain their original source and arithmetic; do not relabel old events to match the current protocol.
{{trim}}{{/if}}{{#if {{getvar::NMPDiceEnabled}}}}MENTAL PROJECTION GROUP 10: World Context & Resolution Bridge
Includes 27.00, 27.01, 27.02, 27.03, 27.04, 27.05, 27.06, 27.07. Cross-references use these source labels; the group, not separate per-field toggles, controls their presence.

RESOLUTION BRIDGE: ONE ATTEMPT, ONE RESULT

MP 27.01-27.07 are active here with the selected Success Dice + Tactical Combat protocol and this component group. Do not create a second randomizer, combat system or independent resolution pass. Reuse the result assigned to this exact attempt by the Success Dice three-slot policy: NemoSuccessRollUser, NemoSuccessRollNPC or NemoSuccessRollFlex, or the already assigned literal result of this exact pending attempt. With dice off, read context normally, retain useful historical resolution records as inactive carryover, and use established facts/plausibility without a fabricated roll.

Choose each real uncertainty from actual intent and character state, before interpreting its assigned value. User owns the first eligible new attempt by the user character; Primary NPC owns the first eligible new attempt by the already identified main NPC; Flex owns the first remaining eligible uncertainty in event order, including another actor, an established environmental event or a genuinely distinct second attempt after its actor's reserved slot is assigned. Each of the three independent current slots can serve at most one new attempt. Keep role reservations fixed, never swap or borrow values, and leave unused slots unused. Trivial, impossible, settled or already-resolved actions consume no fresh slot. Ordinary thought and conversation require no dice. A plausible route and meaningful unsettled result must exist. Keep wanting, willingness, boundaries, identity and another participant's unprovided response out of the die's authority. Each genuinely separate consequential uncertainty needs its own eligible unused slot or separately supplied authoritative result; further acts follow established state/plausibility when no eligible input remains. Do not reuse another actor's luck or invent additional d100 draws. Count opposition once in the owning check's difficulty. Set actor, action, method, specific question, evidence basis, achievable result and plausible consequence scope before interpreting the number. 95+: critical_success; 75-94: strong_success; 50-74: success; 30-49: mixed; 15-29: failure; 5-14: strong_failure; below 5: critical_failure. Critical results remain possible benefits/setbacks of this check, not unrelated catastrophe, unavailable evidence, forced humiliation, consent or personality changes. Internal retrieval can recover only encoded information within fidelity limits; a focused delivery can still be mistaken. When the same internal attempt is modeled in Conscious Workspace, resolve it here once, not again there.

Depict the actual attempt and outcome chronologically. Perceived consequences update their receiving fields once; never apply the die score directly to chemistry, relationship values or map activity. Store used inputs, tier and outcome in the existing owning resolution record; include the literal dice_slot=User, dice_slot=Primary NPC or dice_slot=Flex in qualitative resolution_factors. Use stable resolutions records with actor/action/question/scope/basis, qualitative resolution_factors, the four owned numbers, resolution_tier, outcome, mode, source and status. Preserve optional consequence references and retry condition. Modes remain rolled, automatic, impossible, plausibility or external; statuses resolved, pending or retired. Rolled uses the seven tier keys; otherwise use unrolled and omit/null the four numbers. Source is nemo_success_dice for this integration's current macro-supplied result, external_result for supplied adjudication, or no_roll. Preserve historical post_history_macro records without relabeling them. The new source label is descriptive metadata, not a new score or schema structure.

A pending check retains its assigned roll and context. A retry needs a materially changed method, means, condition or actual cost and a new attempt ID; repeated wording, an unwelcome result, opening the panel or continuing narration is not enough. Do not save unused rolls. A missing/malformed/unexpanded input gives no rolled score: continue with supported plausibility, never invent dice or stall for an absent tool. An unavailable discarded swipe is not secretly remembered; no cross-branch roll locking is claimed. If another focal snapshot includes the same physical result, reference its owning record instead of assigning the current roll again.

Keep the current/most consequential result and genuinely pending checks, then consolidate durable consequences into their existing fields. Reprinting a result does not enact its aftermath again. The renderer only shows authored literal numbers; it does not calculate, validate or repair arithmetic. Keep source registry names and full tracker boundaries stable.


### MP 27.02 | Resolution Raw Roll / Supplied d100
VALUE: Resolution Raw Roll
TRACKER FIELD: resolutions[].resolution_roll
SCALE: Integer 1-100, copied from the role-bound current input assigned to this attempt by Nemo's enabled Success Dice + Tactical Combat module (User, Primary NPC or Flex). null or absence means no recorded random draw, never zero.

DEFINITION
The external pseudorandom input actually assigned to one eligible attempt. It is not a desire score, probability estimate, physiological state or permission. The raw die neither chooses the attempt nor determines the quality without context.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Only resolution_effective for its assigned attempt. It has no direct effect on feelings, choices, weather, unrelated actions, or other characters. No automatic natural-1/natural-100 override is added; use the effective-result bands after eligibility and scope are established.

HOW IT CHANGES
Copy the assigned NemoSuccessRollUser, NemoSuccessRollNPC or NemoSuccessRollFlex integer literally when its new eligible check is used. Keep the actor and slot with the owning record. Never select among roles by value, reuse a consumed slot, swap, reroll, invert, average or improve its number. A new generation can supply a fresh input; it does not overwrite a recorded result for the same attempt. If the same already-recorded pending attempt resumes, preserve its assigned literal roll rather than consuming a fresh one. An unused roll is discarded, not saved for a later opportunity.

INTERACTIONS
MP 27.03 supplies a contextual modifier; MP 27.04 supplies positive difficulty; MP 27.05 performs the arithmetic. The raw value does not alter any of those inputs or select the story's register. A user-supplied authoritative game result is handled as external resolution, not disguised as this slot's random draw.

INITIALIZATION
No seed, midpoint or model-invented random value. Read only the current Success Dice integer assigned to this attempt's User, Primary NPC or Flex slot. Historical records without slot metadata retain their original provenance; never relabel them retroactively. If it is missing, malformed or an unexpanded placeholder, do not produce a rolled check. New checks have no trend arrow; past dice are historical results, not a time series that goes up or down.

TIMESCALE
One assigned attempt. Historical result records use literal numbers only, never executable dice syntax.
### MP 27.03 | Resolution Context Modifier / Relevant Advantages and Costs
VALUE: Resolution Context Modifier
TRACKER FIELD: resolutions[].resolution_modifier
SCALE: Signed integer -40 to 40. 0: no net actor-specific advantage or disadvantage. Normal adjustments lie within -20 to 20; values beyond that require exceptional established support or impairment. null/absence means not applied.

DEFINITION
One bounded net assessment of the actual performer's preparation, established capability, equipment, positioning, help and relevant current condition for this particular attempt. It is not a sum of the tracker stats, moral worth, desire, willingness, or affection.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Adds once to the raw roll in resolution_effective. Positive values help execution; negative values hinder it. List a few material reasons in resolution_factors without introducing separate unowned numerical sub-scores. If opposing conditions balance, 0 is valid and the reasons remain visible.

HOW IT CHANGES
Set from the pre-outcome state and method of the actual attempt. Fatigue can hinder sustained precision; relevant practice can help; a genuinely useful rehearsal may help one line without granting general eloquence. Strong wanting may explain persistence without improving skill. High expressive inhibition is a motive to manage display, not automatic competence at concealment. Do not add a symptom or deficit merely because a stat is high.

INTERACTIONS
Count a causal condition once. Rumination, distraction and reduced task focus may be one source of interference, not three penalties. Task-intrinsic resistance belongs to resolution_difficulty; actor-relative supports belong here. Do not charge an opposing defender's ability twice as both a penalty and difficulty. Perceived feasibility is the character's belief, not a calibrated success probability or a copied bonus. A novice's confidence cannot supply missing training. The same supplied die must not change the modifier.

INITIALIZATION
Use evidence at the point the attempt occurs. If no supported actor-specific effects matter, use 0. Describe uncertainty honestly rather than fabricating exact biological conversion formulas. These bounds are authored game rules, not measured human performance effects.

TIMESCALE
One actual method and contest. Freeze the assigned modifier once the attempt is resolved or its roll is committed; a materially changed later attempt gets its own record.
### MP 27.04 | Resolution Difficulty / Positive Task Pressure
VALUE: Resolution Difficulty
TRACKER FIELD: resolutions[].resolution_difficulty
SCALE: Integer 0-45, always NONNEGATIVE. Larger values make the check harder. null/absence means no d100 difficulty was applied.

DEFINITION
The task's established resistance under current world rules and relevant opposition, expressed as positive pressure subtracted from the raw roll plus context modifier. It is distinct from story danger, the character's perceived feasibility, and the severity of a plausible consequence.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Subtract exactly once in resolution_effective. Do not write a negative difficulty and subtract it, and do not add it. Reference anchors: trivial/near-trivial 0-5 (normally no roll); standard uncertain 5-10; hard 15-25; very hard 25-35; heroic 35-45. Intermediate values are allowed for intermediate resistance; those labels are anchors, not exclusive discrete classes.

HOW IT CHANGES
Set from the actual obstacle, required precision, opposition and established world logic before interpreting the die. A changed route or actual change to opposition can change a later check. A desired dramatic beat, a preferred winner, an impressive raw roll, or mere repetition cannot. In settings where an act is effortless for the established performer, skip the roll instead of forcing an artificial failure chance.

INTERACTIONS
Keep performer-specific advantages in resolution_modifier. Do not penalize the same cause twice. Whether someone will choose to act belongs to willingness and character friction, not a universal persuasion difficulty. An impossible act is not difficulty 45 waiting for a lucky roll; an already-settled act is not an uncertain contest. Follow a directly requested external game system as external resolution rather than silently mixing its arithmetic with this system.

INITIALIZATION
Read current facts, explicit source mechanics and credible opposition. Do not use a negative sign or an arbitrary plot-protection value. When the task is genuinely underspecified, adjudicate only what the supplied information supports; missing knowledge does not authorize hidden obstacles invented to fit the number.

TIMESCALE
One stated check. Inherit an unchanged pending check's difficulty; a reroll request alone does not change it.
### MP 27.05 | Resolution Effective Result / Arithmetic Only
VALUE: Resolution Effective Result
TRACKER FIELD: resolutions[].resolution_effective
SCALE: Integer -84 to 140 with the current raw-roll, modifier and difficulty bounds. It is a game-resolution score, not a percentage. null/absence means no valid d100 calculation occurred.

DEFINITION AND CALCULATION
resolution_effective = resolution_roll + resolution_modifier - resolution_difficulty.
Example arithmetic only: 73 + 10 - 15 = 68. Never copy an example as a live roll. Do not clamp negative results to zero or high results to 100; the outcome bands already cover both ends. Do not invent another bonus, separate fate score, or probability conversion.

WHAT IT AFFECTS
Selects one MP 27.06 outcome band for the already-selected eligible attempt. It does not pick an action, change pre-action desire or willingness, or guarantee consequences outside the question's established scope.

HOW IT CHANGES
Compute exactly from the three recorded numerical inputs. If the recorded arithmetic disagrees, correct the arithmetic and the corresponding band before committing. Do not adjust the inputs to protect the earlier prose. Once a result is established, reprinting or continuing the same attempt is not another calculation. Genuine subsequent consequences can update later state once.

INTERACTIONS
Use all three inputs from the same resolution record. No borrowing a roll from another attempt, a difficulty from another route, or a modifier from another actor. A missing/null input prevents a rolled score. Automatic, impossible, external, and plausibility resolutions use no fabricated effective score.

INITIALIZATION
There is no independent fallback. Derive from one valid, actually assigned die plus its frozen modifier and positive difficulty. Use the plain numeric marker without trend, meter percentage or causal input suggesting the score is another mental pressure.

TIMESCALE
One recorded check. It is a readout of the resolution calculation, not a persistent psychological variable.{{/if}}
{{#if !{{getvar::NMPDiceEnabled}}}}{{#if {{.NemoResolutionProtocol == ttrpg_d20}}}}The generic d100-owned MP 27.01-27.07 VALUE fields are inactive under TTRPG. The native bridge above still records accepted macro/simulated outcomes qualitatively; it does not draw another die. Preserve historical d100 records with their original provenance.{{else}}Success Dice is disabled: MP 27.01-27.07 are inactive, including their four VALUE fields. Keep any necessary historical resolutions as inactive carryover; do not roll or create new dice state.{{/if}}{{/if}}{{/if}}
{{/if}}
{{trim}}{{/setvar}}{{trim}}

prompts.name: 🧩 Dreamscape · MP Clock Ownership
prompts.content:
{{// @category Mental-Projection }}{{// @tooltip Automatic Dreamscape clock ownership for Mental Projection. Stores a compatibility directive only when Dreamscape and MP coexist. }}{{// @icon 🌫️ }}{{// @badge AUTO }}{{// @hidden }}
{{setvar::NDTActive::0}}{{setvar::NDTMPDirective::}}{{#if {{getvar::NemoWorldMod_v11_155_world_augments_dreamscape_reality}}}}{{setvar::NDTActive::1}}{{/if}}
{{#if {{getvar::NDTActive}}}}{{#if {{getvar::NMPEnabled}}}}{{#setvar::NDTMPDirective}}
DREAMSCAPE TIME OWNERSHIP
Dreamscape may make experienced duration diverge from the shared material clock. Distinguish them only when the fiction actually establishes a divergence; otherwise use one ordinary elapsed interval and do not manufacture dilation.

- WORLD ELAPSED: diegetic material time shared with bodies, outside locations and ordinary simultaneous threads. Passive physiology, wound healing, hunger/thirst, drug metabolism, sleep debt, equipment processes and other material-time effects use this clock unless established dream physics explicitly transfer or replace them.
- EXPERIENCED DURATION: the subjective sequence lived inside the relevant dream layer. Thoughts, appraisals, memories, fear, desire, decisions and other genuinely experienced events may change Mental Projection because those events occurred to that mind, even when little world time passed. Do not multiply passive body/chemistry decay or recovery merely because the dream felt long.

A dream event is one cause, not one cause per apparent hour. Apply actual experienced events through their normal MP definitions and causal scopes. Long subjective duration alone does not manufacture repeated stress, relationship gains, skill practice, nutrition, wound healing or hormone changes. Repetition requires repeated experienced events; passive change requires the clock owned by that field.

MEMORY AND SEQUENCE
A memory formed in a long subjective sequence may contain that internal order and felt duration while still being recent on the world clock. Keep sequence/experienced-age separate from objective timestamp or outside elapsed time. Do not falsify world chronology to make the memory feel old, and do not erase the experienced sequence because only a breath passed outside.

WAKING / CROSS-LAYER EFFECTS
Dreamscape already permits fear, injury, desire, revelations or bargains to leave marks after waking when the setting supports that. Carry across only the consequences established by the active world rules and actual event. Do not automatically export dream-body fatigue, resources, healing, damage or elapsed hours into the waking body. Conversely, a supported persistent psychological or supernatural consequence remains real even if the outside interval was brief.

When continuity needs the distinction, keep a concise clock relation in the existing story_context/continuity note rather than creating a second state engine or new numeric meter. State which layer/clock owns an effect only when ambiguity matters. Narrative Stage held-turn counts remain accepted-reply bookkeeping and are never converted into dream years or world elapsed time.
{{/setvar}}{{/if}}{{/if}}{{trim}}
